title: OASIS: Object-Aware Page Management for Multi-GPU Systems
problem: Unified Virtual Memory (UVM) in multi-GPU systems applies a single, application-object-agnostic page placement and migration policy to all data, failing to account for the fact that different data objects and different execution phases of the same object benefit from different page management strategies.
motivation: As multi-GPU systems scale to handle larger deep learning workloads, UVM's one-size-fits-all page management causes unnecessary migrations, missed duplication opportunities, and suboptimal data locality, leaving significant performance on the table.
method: OASIS watches how your data is accessed while the program runs, using hardware counters—essentially tallies of memory reads and writes—to figure out what access patterns each piece of data follows across different execution phases. For each piece of data in each phase, it picks the best handling strategy: on-touch migration (moving data to a GPU only when it's first accessed there), access-counter-based migration (moving data based on observed usage patterns), or duplication (keeping copies on multiple GPUs). The system coordinates between software and hardware to automatically switch strategies when the program moves into a new phase, without requiring any manual programmer annotation.
key_novelty: OASIS automatically picks the best page management approach for each piece of data based on its actual runtime usage patterns and current execution phase in multi-GPU systems, choosing between migration (moving data to GPUs) and duplication (keeping copies across GPUs).
contributions: Characterization of object-level page access behavior variation across application objects and execution phases in multi-GPU workloads
OASIS: a dynamic runtime system for object-granularity, phase-adaptive page management policy selection
64% improvement over on-touch migration, 35% over access-counter migration, 42% over duplication
12% improvement over state-of-the-art GRIT with significantly lower design complexity

metrics.speedup: 64% over on-touch migration; 35% over access-counter migration; 42% over duplication; 12% over GRIT

limitations: The object-pattern detection overhead and the scope of object types that can be accurately identified at runtime are not quantified in the abstract.
primary_theme: Object-aware adaptive page management for multi-GPU unified virtual memory
